{
  "title": "RULE-BASED GRAPH PROGRAMS MATCHING THE TIME COMPLEXITY OF IMPERATIVE ALGORITHMS",
  "research_problem": "Rule-based graph transformation languages generally fail to achieve the asymptotic runtime efficiency of imperative languages due to the cost of graph matching. Previous work with rooted rules could match imperative time complexity but required input graphs to have bounded node degree and, for some algorithms, to be connected. This paper addresses these limitations.",
  "motivation": "Matching the lefthand graph L of a rule within a host graph G generally requires time |G|^|L|, so standard imperative graph algorithms running in linear time may exhibit nonlinear, polynomial runtimes when recast as rule-based graph programs. Existing GP 2 programs with rooted rules needed bounded node degree and connectivity constraints. Overcoming these constraints enables linear-time and O(nm)-time rule-based graph programs on arbitrary input graphs.",
  "main_contribution": "The paper enhances the graph data structure generated by the GP 2 compiler by storing nodes in separate linked lists based on marks and incident edges in a two-dimensional array of linked lists based on marks and orientation. Three case studies are presented: (1) a GP 2 program checking connectedness in linear time on arbitrary input graphs, (2) a program recognising acyclic graphs in linear time, and (3) a rule-based implementation of Bellman-Ford single-source shortest-path algorithm running in O(nm) time, matching imperative complexity. Each comes with correctness and time complexity proofs and runtime experiments.",
  "methodology": {
    "method_name": "Enhanced GP 2 compiler with improved graph data structure",
    "core_idea": "Nodes are stored in separate linked lists based on their marks (red, green, blue, grey or unmarked), and each node has a two-dimensional array of linked lists storing all incident edges based on their marks (red, green, blue, dashed or unmarked) and orientation (incoming, outgoing or looping). This enables the matching algorithm to find in constant time a node with a specific mark or an edge with a specific mark and orientation.",
    "pipeline": "GP 2 programs are compiled to C programs using the GP 2-to-C compiler. C programs are transformed by GCC into platform-dependent binaries. Binaries are executed by the runtime system which reads an input graph from disc.",
